checks.basis: inspect now retains the exact app source. Only a stable lexical helper binding to a one-literal-argument call of the owner webpack third parameter is accepted; mutated/shadowed require/helper identifiers are rejected by existing guards. The requested literal ID must identify exactly one literal-key AST Property value. It must be a FunctionExpression whose complete source slice SHA equals the independently pinned 300-byte module. That exact pin entails one module parameter and the observed helper export; no generalized external-helper trust is added. Unknown, changed or duplicate candidates fail closed. Local-helper recognition is unchanged.

Full current compatibility source factory is used, not a marker substitute. Independent literal helper equals the SDK evidence byte-for-byte and has the exact complete SHA. Requested module IDs 143 and 714 both pass. Each preserves app/input/non-target resource bytes, unchanged page prefix/suffix and original map source; VM checks show no eager factory call and exact identity/protocol/engine reference order on the lazy owner call. Malicious-return drift, missing requested ID and ambiguous literal ID reject without input mutation. All claims remain syntheticQA=true, actualSDKVerified=false and nativeVerified=false.
